transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-11-18
Start: 16:00 PST
Duration: ~52 minutes
Attendees: Jesse (Redwood AE), Ravi (Redwood SE), Monica (Redwood SE), Dana (Avalon Head of ML), Tom (Avalon Infra), Priya (Avalon Security), Evan (Avalon PM)

Auto-summary (auto-generated, may be rough):
Redwood and Avalon scoped a 6-week POC to evaluate hosted vs dedicated vs private deployments. Primary success criteria: p95 latency targets, cost per 1M tokens, and data residency/security constraints. Action items: share benchmarking template, traffic samples, run initial latency+throughput tests on hosted, then compare Dedicated configs.

Topics: success criteria; workload sizing; benchmark plan; timeline; security/VPC/K M S; decision criteria for deployment mode; next steps

Transcript:
[00:00:12] Jesse: Hey everyone, thanks for joining — I think we have about 50 minutes, appreciate you making the time. Quick intros?
[00:00:22] Dana: Hi, I'm Dana, head of ML at Avalon. We run clinical summarization workflows and a patient triage assistant. We're looking at inference infra for production.
[00:00:35] Tom: Tom here, infra. We'll own the network and deployment side.
[00:00:39] Priya: Priya, security lead. We'll want to validate compliance, K M S, audit log retention.
[00:00:45] Evan: Evan, product — mostly coordinating requirements and timelines.
[00:00:50] Jesse: Great. On Redwood side I'm Jesse, AE; Ravi and Monica are our SEs. The goal today is to scope a POC that lets you decide hosting mode — hosted API, Dedicated reserved capacity, or Private (VPC/on-prem). We'll surface benchmarks, success criteria, and a recommended timeline.
[00:01:10] Ravi: Quick clarifying Q: what's your current qps and latency targets for the triage flow? And do you have a preferred model family?
[00:01:20] Dana: We run two workloads: batch summarization (medium throughput, 10-20 reqs/s) and an interactive triage assistant (spiky, peaks up to 400 concurrent sessions, p95 under 300 ms desired). For models, we're experimenting with a 13B open model and a fine-tuned 7B variant for triage.
[00:01:41] Monica: Ok, that mix is very typical — batch vs low-latency interactive. For triage, p95 300ms is doable but depends on model size and batching. If you need <200ms we often recommend Dedicated or Private with inferred quantization.
[00:01:58] Dana: Important note: for any patient data we need at-rest encryption and customer-managed keys. Also data residency in our US-west region.
[00:02:08] Priya: And SOC2 plus formal audit logs for every request mapping back to API keys. We also need RBAC and SSO.
[00:02:15] Jesse: Understood. That drives private or dedicated more likely, but let's map tradeoffs.

[00:02:30] Evan: Can you run through benchmark phases you'd recommend?
[00:02:34] Ravi: Sure — phase 1: quick hosted smoke tests using a representative subset of prompts to measure baseline latency and tokens/sec. Phase 2: Dedicated capacity tests with our standard queueing and batching to see steady-state throughput and cost per token. Phase 3: Private deployment (VPC) for final validation of network egress, K M S and audit log ingestion. Each phase includes both latency and quality checks (we compare outputs to your golden prompts).
[00:03:00] Dana: How long does each phase usually take?
[00:03:03] Monica: Usually 3-7 days per phase if we have your sample data. For a 6-week POC, we compress hosted+dedicated into the first 3 weeks and private verification in the last 2-3 weeks.
[00:03:16] Tom: For Private we need to know infra requirements — GPU types, network ports, NAT, our firewall. Can you provide a deployment checklist?
[00:03:26] Ravi: Yes, we'll share a Private deployment checklist and a sample Terraform snippet. Note: Dedicated uses our managed pools so infra work is minimal on your side.

[00:03:40] [00:03:40] Dana: On cost, we need ballpark numbers for monthly spend at 100k queries/month and peak-day traffic — can you model both hosted and dedicated?
[00:03:52] Jesse: We'll send a cost model spreadsheet. Quick rule-of-thumb: hosted is lower upfront friction but per-token unit cost is higher for sustained throughput; Dedicated yields lower unit cost once you hit reserved commit levels. Private has higher setup/ops but gives control and often required for strict compliance.
[00:04:12] Priya: For audit concerns: can Redwood stream audit logs to our Splunk? Also key rotation policies — we run quarterly rotations.
[00:04:21] Monica: We support streaming logs to customer S3 or SIEMs; Splunk via Kinesis or S3 ingestion is common. K M S integrations are with major cloud providers; quarterly rotation is compatible. We'll include sample configs.

[00:04:38] [00:04:38] Evan: Decision criteria — what should our rubric look like?
[00:04:42] Ravi: We usually recommend scoring across: security/compliance fit, latency SLOs, cost at 6-12 months, operational burden, and timeline to production. Example: if security is mandatory and timeline is >8 weeks, Private may be chosen; if you need <2 week proof-of-concept and lower friction, start with Hosted. If you need predictable per-token cost and sustained high throughput, Dedicated likely wins.
[00:05:10] Dana: One subtlety: our triage assistant processes PHI at times — can hosted be approved if we use token redaction or partial anonymization?
[00:05:20] Priya: We prefer not to rely on redaction as the only control. If hosted is used, we need strong contractual commitments around data usage and retention.
[00:05:28] Jesse: Totally. The POC can validate anonymization patterns but for production we expect either Private or Dedicated with clear retention settings. We'll include retention SLA options in the docs.

[00:05:45] [00:05:45] Tom: For the benchmarks, what metrics should we capture besides p95 latency?
[00:05:50] Monica: p50/p95/p99 latency, tokens/sec, GPU utilization, cost per 1M tokens, failure rates, tail queueing delays, and model output divergence vs your golden set. Also keycard: KV cache hit-rate if you use prefix caching.
[00:06:07] Dana: What about warm-start/kv cache behavior for long sessions? Our triage uses multi-turn context up to 1k tokens.
[00:06:14] Ravi: We'll measure KV cache effectiveness and memory footprint. For multi-turn, the runtime's KV cache reduces repeated compute; Dedicated/Private let you size KV memory more aggressively. Hosted has shared caches and may evict more often under noisy neighbor conditions.
[00:06:32] Evan: Noisy neighbor — so for predictable latency Dedicated helps because of reserved GPU pool?
[00:06:37] Monica: Exactly. Dedicated gives you isolated pools and predictable scheduling. Hosted does soft isolation via routing policies but cannot guarantee the same tail latency.

[00:06:51] [00:06:51] Priya: Governance question: are audit logs tamper-evident? If we stream logs to S3, is there a signature chain?
[00:06:59] Jesse: We provide request-level logs with hashed IDs; for full tamper-evidence you'll want logs in your own vaulted S3 + object locking; we'll document the recommended pattern.
[00:07:12] Tom: Network egress: do you require outbound internet for model weights updates in Private?
[00:07:18] Ravi: Private can be air-gapped if you accept manual updates; for managed Private we have a control-plane connection that can be peered, but offline/on-prem is possible with a packaged release. We'll detail the tradeoffs.

[00:07:34] [00:07:34] Dana: Let's assign POC success criteria concretely. I'll propose the following:
[00:07:39] Dana: 1) Interactive triage: p95 <= 300ms for 90% of peak-day traffic patterns; no data leaves US-west region; keys are customer-managed.
[00:07:50] Dana: 2) Batch summarization: sustained throughput of 200 reqs/s with avg latency per request under 2s and cost per 1k requests under X (TBD in spreadsheet).
[00:08:02] Dana: 3) Model fidelity: outputs within 5% BLEU-ish proxy vs golden set or equivalent QA pass rate above 95% on sample prompts.
[00:08:12] Jesse: That looks good. We'll translate the cost target to actual numbers once we get your traffic sample and tokenization profile.

[00:08:25] [00:08:25] Evan: On timelines — can we do initial hosted smoke test in a week?
[00:08:29] Jesse: Yes, if you provide samples asap. We'll run hosted tests day 1-3, then Dedicated eval days 4-14 depending on commit and pool allocation; Private validation after infra prep, likely week 4-6.
[00:08:44] Tom: For Dedicated we need to know GPU types — A10G vs A100 tradeoffs?
[00:08:50] Monica: For 13B models, A10G is cost-effective for many quantized paths; A100 gives headroom and better throughput for large context lengths. We'll benchmark both if needed.
[00:09:04] Dana: Regarding fallbacks — what happens if Dedicated pool saturates?
[00:09:08] Ravi: We have routing policies: we can failover to hosted-compatible model variants or scale burst capacity if configured. For POC we'll simulate saturation scenarios.

[00:09:22] [00:09:22] Priya: Legal needs: can you provide an SOW template that includes breach notification timelines and data handling clauses?
[00:09:29] Jesse: Yes, legal will share an SOW + data processing addendum for review — we'll include breach notification windows and retention commitments.

[00:09:40] Evan: Any gotchas running benchmarks: offline vs online?
[00:09:44] Ravi: Important to run both: offline (replayed trace) to test throughput and warm-cache behavior; and online synthetic load to test real latencies and tail behavior. Also include cold-starts for session-based flows.
[00:09:58] Dana: We'll provide a 48-hour trace and a synthetic load profile.

[00:10:05] [00:10:05] Jesse: Recap and decisions: 6-week POC, phases hosted (smoke) -> Dedicated (throughput + cost) -> Private (security + final). Primary success: triage p95 <=300ms, batch throughput 200req/s, cost and fidelity targets to be quantified. Action items: we'll exchange samples and templates.
[00:10:28] Monica: I'll attach the benchmark harness repo and runbook; it's lightweight and uses a small client to run traces and capture GPU telemetry.
[00:10:36] Tom: For Private infra checklist, include required open ports, NAT, and IAM roles.

[00:10:45] [00:10:45] Priya: Quick follow-up: do you support customer-managed K M S in Hosted?
[00:10:50] Jesse: Hosted supports envelope encryption and bringing your own key with limited patterns; Dedicated/Private give more flexible K M S ownership models. We'll document exact patterns.

[00:11:05] Evan: Are there preview features for quantization or compiler optimizations we should be aware of?
[00:11:10] Ravi: Yes, we have quantized execution paths and kernel selection that we can enable for Dedicated and Private. On Hosted some of those are available but not all experimental optimizations. We'll call out expected perf delta in the benchmark.

[00:11:26] [00:11:26] Dana: If we move forward with Dedicated, what's typical lead time?
[00:11:30] Monica: If capacity is available, 1-2 weeks to provision pools and run initial smoke tests. If you want dedicated GPUs committed for a month or more, our capacity planning may take longer depending on region.
[00:11:43] Tom: Any dependencies on our cloud account for Dedicated?
[00:11:46] Jesse: Dedicated is managed by Redwood; you don't need to give us cloud account access. For Private, we'll need network peering and IAM roles.

[00:11:58] [00:11:58] Dana: Can you show an example decision rubric?
[00:12:02] Ravi: I'll share one. High-level: if security critical AND low tolerance for external control -> Private; if high throughput and cost sensitivity -> Dedicated; if time-to-prototype is critical -> Hosted. We'll populate a scored matrix in the POC doc.

[00:12:18] Evan: Let's talk benchmarks specifics: sample size, tokenization, failure injection points.
[00:12:22] Monica: We'll ask for representative prompt sets, expected context windows, and target concurrency. We'll run tokenized histograms, and inject latency on the control-plane to see behavior. Also run cold-cache vs warm-cache runs.
[00:12:36] Dana: For model fidelity threshold, we don't strictly use BLEU but a domain-specific QA pass/fail; we'll provide scoring script.

[00:12:45] [00:12:45] Jesse: Great. Any other concerns?
[00:12:48] Priya: Data residency enforcement at rest and in transit — please include certs for encryption in transit?
[00:12:54] Monica: We'll include TLS and mTLS patterns, plus region-specific storage controls in the doc.

[00:13:05] [00:13:05] Evan: I'll block time to review the cost model with finance.
[00:13:09] Dana: Timeline check — can legal review SOW in two weeks if we get the draft this week?
[00:13:13] Jesse: Yes, we'll aim to send SOW and security docs within 48 hours after this call.

[00:13:22] [00:13:22] Ravi: Quick note on metrics collection: we'll instrument GPU counters, per-request timings, and provide a dashboard. If you want Splunk/SIEM integration, we can forward logs or give a sidecar shipper.
[00:13:36] Tom: That works.

[00:13:40] Monica: We'll prepare a short benchmark runbook with the exact command-lines so your infra team can repro locally if desired.

[00:13:48] [00:13:48] Jesse: Thanks everyone — final recap of next steps: Redwood to send benchmark template, cost model, SOW and security artifacts; Avalon to send traffic samples and compliance questions. We'll schedule the infra deep-dive next week.
[00:14:02] Dana: Sounds good.
[00:14:05] Evan: Thanks all.
[00:14:07] Jesse: End of recorded portion — remainder of call was around scheduling and some quick Q&A not captured cleanly in the transcript.
